title: tf-module-release-scenario-matrix
summary: Working matrix and lightweight playbook for publishing tf modules used in private/on-prem deployments. Focuses on deciding version bumps, prepublish verification, registry tagging, and safe rollout/rollback signals for customers running pinned module versions.
purpose: Provide engineers and release coordinators a concise scenario-driven checklist for module versioning, registry publish steps, and broken-change mitigations specific to on-prem and VPC module consumers.
background: We have a growing number of Terraform modules consumed by Private deployments customers. Modules evolve (bugfixes, features, refactors). Historically we've had ad-hoc publishes that caused unexpected provider changes for customers pinned to major versions. This doc proposes a scenario matrix, explicit prepublish tests, and a minimal comms + rollback playbook tailored to private/onprem usage patterns.
goals: Minimize breaking changes for customers running pinned module versions
Automate prepublish compatibility tests against representative stacks
Define clear rollback triggers and quick mitigations for field regressions
Reduce cognitive load on release engineers during module publishes
release_scenarios: Patch: non-API bugfix (no input/output surface change) -> patch bump (x.y.z)
Minor: additive change (new optional inputs, new resources behind feature flag) -> minor bump (x.y+1.0)
Major: breaking change (rename inputs/outputs, remove resources, change semantic behavior) -> major bump (x+1.0.0) and migration guide
Refactor-with-backcompat: internal refactor that preserves inputs/outputs but may change resource addresses -> minor bump after compatibility tests
Internal dependency upgrade: upstream provider or module bump that may be breaking -> evaluate with test matrix; often minor or major depending on surface impact
compatibility_tests: Unit lint + fmt (tflint, terraform fmt, checkov)
Integration apply against small sample stacks used in private deployments (vpc-setup, onprem-k8s-bootstrap, dedicated-gpu-pool) using pinned provider versions
Acceptance: run terraform plan/apply/plan twice (idempotency) and verify no drift after apply+destroy
State-migration smoke: run upgrade from previous released version (x.y.z -> candidate) in ephemeral workspace with representative state snapshot
Policy checks: run compliance policy suite (RDW-policies) to ensure no new infra patterns flagged
prepublish_checks: All tests in CI green and artifacts uploaded to CI storage
CHANGELOG entry describing user-impact, migration steps, and opt-in flags
Docs update: README input/output table reviewed
Automation: release pipeline job configured to publish tag + registry entry
Stakeholder review: solutions-eng and SRE sign-off for modules used by Dedicated/Private customers
publish_steps: Create release branch and bump version in module manifest (semver)
Run full CI integration matrix (see compatibility_tests) against branch
Merge to main when CI green and approvals obtained
Create signed git tag <module>-vX.Y.Z and push
Trigger registry publish job (terraform registry or internal artifact registry)
Attach CHANGELOG, migration notes, and compatibility matrix to the registry entry
Notify stakeholders via release Slack channel and post Confluence shortnote
rollout_playbook: Stage publish as 'canary' (internal flag consumers and non-critical customers) for 48 hours
Monitor telemetry: module-related incidents, CI signals, SRE error budgets, and customer support tickets
If no regressions, promote to general availability; otherwise follow rollback_triggers
For major bumps, coordinate with customer success to contact high-risk customers with migration timelines and optional mitigation patches
rollback_triggers: Reproducible apply failures observed in >=2 independent environments within 6 hours
State corruption or resource address drift detected during smoke migrations
Customer-reported production outage attributable to module change
Breaking API change missing migration docs and causing inability to plan/apply
communications_timeline: T-48h: internal announce to eng-private-deployments + solutions-eng with release notes
T+0h: publish registry entry (canary) and post Slack note to #releases
T+24h: short status update; if canary healthy, recommend GA in 24h
On rollback: immediate @channel notification, include mitigation steps and who to contact
Postmortem within 72h if rollback or customer impact occurred
versioning_policy: Adopt semantic versioning with conservative major bumps. Default to patch for bug fixes, minor for additive/backwards-compatible features, major for breaking API changes. For changes that only affect internal behavior but could surface resource address changes, err toward minor and include migration notes.
deprecation_policy: When deprecating resources/inputs: mark deprecated in docs for at least two release cycles, add runtime deprecation warnings where possible, provide automated migration script or example, and communicate directly with customers who have pinned older majors.
notes_to_self: Next steps: wire this matrix into the release pipeline as a checklist step; add a small suite of representative state snapshots in the infra-cassettes repo; schedule 30-min working session with Solutions Eng to agree on 'canary' customer list. Consider automating semantic-bump suggestion from change summary in PRs.
